title: rostrum project
description: A rostrum project: one talk or a whole event. `defaults` apply to every talk; each talk can override any settings key.

$schema.description: Schema URL, for editor autocomplete and validation.

event.description: Event name, shown in reports and usable in output names.

talks.description: Talks in this project, in queue order.

level.description: auto: shown with cut pre-selected. propose: shown with keep pre-selected. off: not run.

talk.description: One talk: one or more source files in order. Any settings key overrides `defaults` for this talk.

id.description: Talk id: letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore.

sources.description: Source files in order, relative to the project file. They form one timeline.

speaker.description: Speaker name, used by the output name template.

title.description: Talk title, used by the output name template.

settingsFile.description: A settings object on its own (project defaults, ~/.rostrum/config.json).

path.description: Talk script as a text file, relative to the project file. Lines starting with # are headings.

sectionPattern.description: Heading that starts a section (group 1 is the section number).

spokenHeading.description: When a section has this heading, only the text after it is spoken.

skipLines.description: Lines matching these patterns are not spoken.

settings.description: Settings. Layers, later wins: built-in defaults, ~/.rostrum/config.json, project defaults, talk, CLI flags.

workDir.description: Work folder for a talk, relative to the project file. {talk} is the talk id.

engine.description: Engine name: faster-whisper, command, import, or a plugin from the rostrum.engines entry-point group.

model.description: faster-whisper model name or local model folder.

language.description: Spoken language code; null lets the engine detect it.

prompt.description: Initial prompt for the engine. When null and hints are set, the hints are used.

hints.description: Names and terms the engine should expect (prompt and hotwords).

computeType.description: faster-whisper compute type. auto: int8 on CPU, float16 on CUDA.

workers.description: Parallel transcription workers, or auto: min(max(1, CPUs // 4), available RAM GB // 2, 6). Each model copy needs about 1-2 GB of memory.

threadsPerWorker.description: CPU threads for each worker's model, or auto: the CPUs divided by the workers, at least 1.

vadMinSilenceMs.description: Voice activity filter: shortest silence that splits speech.

chunkSec.description: Length of each parallel transcription chunk.

overlapSec.description: Audio overlap on each side of a chunk.

chunkSearchSec.description: How far from the nominal chunk end to look for a silence to split at.

chunkMinSilenceSec.description: Shortest silence used as a chunk split point.

retryEcho.description: Re-transcribe, without the prompt, segments where the engine echoed its prompt.

echoMinWords.description: Consecutive prompt words that mark a segment as an echo.

cuePass.description: Second pass without voice filtering to catch short spoken cues (engines that support it).

cueScope.description: full: the whole timeline in overlapping cueWindowSec windows. targeted: only short windows around a burst of sound in a gap between words or a span the main pass got wrong; on a short clip with few gaps it is faster, but the model often misses a word near the start of a short window, so it finds fewer cues.

cueFallback.description: Let the cue pass retry hard audio at higher temperatures. Off: one decode per window at temperature 0, so noise and silence cost one decode, not six, and the result is the same on every run.

cueGapSec.description: targeted: gaps between main-pass words at least this long are checked for sound.

cueSoundSec.description: targeted: shortest burst of sound in a gap that gets a cue window.

cuePadSec.description: targeted: audio kept around each place, for context.

cueMergeSec.description: targeted: places closer than this share a window.

cueEdgeSec.description: Words this close to an inner window edge are taken from the neighbouring window.

cueWords.description: Words the cue pass adds to the transcript when the main pass missed them.

command.description: command engine: program and arguments. Placeholders: {audio} (a 16 kHz mono WAV of the source, on the source's clock), {input} (the source file itself), {output}, {language}, {model}. Prefer {audio}: when a source's audio starts late, only {audio} is padded so word times line up with the video; a tool that reads {input} would time its words from the audio start. On Windows, a .bat or .cmd program, or cmd itself, gets no argument with & ^ % ! < > | or a quote.

format.description: command and import engines: transcript format.

timeoutSec.description: command engine: time limit per source; null means no limit.

transcripts.description: import engine: one transcript per source, relative to the project file. Empty: look for <source stem>.words.json, .json, .srt or .vtt next to the source.

fields.description: Field mapping for JSON transcripts. Paths use dots; [] flattens a list (segments[].words[]).

timeScale.description: Multiply times by this to get seconds (0.001 for milliseconds).

transcript.description: How words are grouped and shown.

sentenceEnd.description: Characters that end a sentence unit.

unitGapSec.description: A silence this long also ends a sentence unit.

longWordSec.description: Words longer than this are trimmed to their loud frames.

failedPadSec.description: Margin around ranges where transcription failed.

unclearBelow.description: Words below this probability show as [unclear] in evidence.

contextWords.description: Words of evidence before and after a cut.

audio.description: Loudness analysis used to place cut edges in quiet frames.

floorPercentile.description: Noise floor: this percentile of frame loudness.

peakPercentile.description: Speech peak: this percentile of frame loudness.

silenceLevel.description: Silence threshold, as a share of the way from floor to peak.

speechLevel.description: Speech threshold, as a share of the way from floor to peak.

text.description: Word lists used to compare sentences.

stopWords.description: Words ignored when comparing the key words of two sentences.

discourseWords.description: Words skipped at the start of a sentence when checking for a restarted phrase.

cues.description: Spoken cues such as "redo" or "stop". The cut goes back to where the abandoned attempt started.

patterns.description: Cue phrases (regular expressions on lower-case words). Low-confidence phrases are proposed unless an abandoned attempt is found before them.

words.description: Single words that start a stand-alone cue ("Stop.", "Redo, okay."). Matched case-insensitively without punctuation; put phrases in patterns.

endWords.description: Single words that end a stand-alone cue ("Okay, stop.").

companionWords.description: Other single words allowed inside a stand-alone cue.

trailingWords.description: A sentence ending in one of these single words, then a silence, is a cue too.

trailingGapSec.description: Silence needed after a trailing cue word.

phraseLookbackSec.description: Cue phrases: how far back to look for the abandoned attempt.

lookbackSec.description: Stand-alone cues: how far back to look for the abandoned attempt.

resaidWindowSec.description: An earlier sentence is part of the abandoned attempt only if it is said again within this time after the cue.

resaidShare.description: Share of a sentence's key words that must be said again.

resaidMinWords.description: Key words that must be said again (unless the sentence has only one).

retakes.description: A sentence said again within the window. Strong matches are cut; loose matches are proposed. A sentence said again with swapped words gets substitutionLevel instead.

substitutionLevel.description: For a sentence said again with swapped words (“page before the change”, then “page after the change”): deliberate parallel phrasing or a spoken correction, so it is proposed with keep selected. auto: cut it like any retake. off: never treat it as a retake. A restart or an extension of the earlier sentence keeps level.

substitutionMaxWords.description: Longest swap, in words on each side, that still counts as a substitution. A longer change between the shared words makes the pair a rewording, which keeps level.

windowSec.description: Longest time between an attempt and its retake.

ngram.description: Word n-gram size for a quick shared-phrase check.

strongRun.description: Shared run of words that makes a strong match.

shortRun.description: A shorter shared run also counts when it covers shortRunShare of the attempt.

scriptedRunMax.description: Words of the shared run checked against the script.

scriptedLimit.description: A shared run found in this many script sentences is a planned repeat, not a retake.

shortRatio.description: Similarity that makes two short sentences a strong match.

prefixMaxWords.description: A short sentence that the next sentence starts with is a false start.

sharedWords.description: Shared key words for a loose match.

nearSharedWords.description: Shared key words for a loose match within nearSec.

scriptSame.description: Script match that puts two sentences on the same script line.

scriptConflict.description: Script match that puts two sentences on different script lines (not a retake).

scriptMapped.description: Script match that marks a sentence as scripted.

guardRegionMinSec.description: Everything cut must be said again within max(this, guardRegionFactor x attempt length) after the retake.

guardRetakeUnits.description: Sentences at the retake whose key words cover cut sentences.

asideMaxWords.description: Sentences up to this long next to an aside can be cut with it.

unclearBelow.description: Short sentences below this mean word probability can be cut with a retake.

repeats.description: A restarted phrase inside one sentence ("we shipped it on, shipped it on Friday").

ngram.description: Repeated words that mark a restart.

extraWords.description: Words after the restart that must contain every key word of the dropped part.

prefixMinLength.description: A dropped word this long also matches a longer word that starts with it.

pauses.description: Dead air over maxSec is trimmed to keepSec on each side.

islandMarginSec.description: Loud sounds inside a pause (a click, a breath) split it; this margin is ignored at each end.

leads.description: Dead air at the start and end of the talk.

minProbability.description: First and last words must be at least this clear.

offtalk.description: Short asides that are not part of the talk ("Is this recording?").

okWords.description: Words that may fill a clear aside besides strongWords and stop words.

greetingWords.description: A sentence with these words is a greeting to the audience, not an aside.

fillers.description: Filler words. The list is always used to compare sentences; the detector is off by default.

unclear.description: Stretches the transcript cannot be trusted: an overlong word, a run of low-confidence words, a segment the engine was unsure of or that reads like a known hallucination, speech with no words, or a range where transcription failed. They are proposed for a listen, and retake and cue matching never joins words across them.

maxWordSec.description: A word whose sound lasts longer than this is unclear (the engine stretched it over something it did not transcribe). Measured on the word's loud frames.

minProbability.description: Words below this probability are low-confidence.

minSec.description: A run of low-confidence words this long is unclear.

maxAvgLogprob.description: A segment whose average log-probability is below this is unclear.

untranscribedSec.description: A gap between words holding at least this much speech-level sound is unclear: speech the engine did not transcribe.

default: see you in the next video
hallucinationPhrases.description: A segment containing one of these phrases is unclear, and its words are not matched.

mergeGapSec.description: Unclear stretches closer than this are proposed as one. Also the longest pause inside a run of low-confidence words.

breakSentences.description: Unclear stretches break sentences: retake, cue, repeat and off-talk matching never joins words across their edges, and the words of untrusted stretches (an overlong word, a segment that reads like a hallucination) stand alone and are not matched. Off: match exactly as the original rules did.

edges.description: Where a cut edge goes between two words: the quietest frame near the gap.

plan.description: How candidates become the cut list.

minPieceSec.description: Smaller pieces of overlapping cuts are dropped.

minKeepSec.description: Kept pieces shorter than this, with no word in them, are cut too.

maxProposalSec.description: Longer low-confidence candidates are not proposed.

coveredShare.description: Proposals already this covered by cuts are dropped.

reconcile.description: Second pass: cut loose retakes that are said again later, cut back from stand-alone cues, and use slide evidence when a slide timeline is set.

maxSpanSec.description: Longest attempt-to-retake span for a loose retake.

sameOpeningWords.description: Attempt and retake starting with the same words count as the same sentence.

firstUnitShare.description: Key words of the first cut sentence that must be said again.

unitShare.description: Key words of every other cut sentence that must be said again.

unitCutShare.description: A sentence this covered by cuts counts as cut.

resaidMinWords.description: Key words that must be said again (unless the sentence has only one).

abortedShare.description: A slide visit is an aborted start when this share of its sentences is said again later.

flashSec.description: A slide shown for less than this between other slides is a flash.

slides.description: Optional slide evidence from an existing slide timeline (slides.timeline). The slide check flags back-jumps and flashes; slide-based cuts are proposed by default. Matching slides from a deck is not in 0.1: the other keys are reserved.

deck.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Slide deck (PDF or a folder of images).

timeline.description: Existing slide-timeline outputs: a path prefix (<folder>/<label>) or a -timeline.csv file; a list gives one per source.

threshold.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: correlation needed to name a slide.

sampleFps.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: frames sampled per second.

crop.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: slide area [x, y, width, height] in video pixels; null finds it.

titleRows.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: rows of the 144-row slide image used to name the slide.

bodyRows.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: rows used to measure reveal progress.

finalMinSec.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: the final pass of a slide is its last visit at least this long.

shortVisitSec.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: a visit shorter than this is a flash.

transitionMaxSec.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: longest slide transition.

revealTolerance.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: reveal progress noise to ignore.

revealMinStep.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: smallest reveal step.

rewindMin.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: smallest reveal rewind.

maxOffSec.description: Reserved; not used in 0.1. Matching: longest time with no slide in view.

script.description: Optional talk script: a path, or {path, sectionPattern, spokenHeading, skipLines}. Matching sentences against it tells a retake from a planned repeat. Off when no path is set.

crf.description: x264 quality (lower is better); null leaves it to the encoder.

audioRate.description: Audio sample rate of the output.

container.description: Output container: mp4, mkv or mov.

loudnessLufs.description: EBU R128 loudness target; null leaves loudness alone.

normalizeVfr.description: Convert variable frame rate sources to constant frame rate first.

mode.description: fast checks timestamps at every join and samples A/V offset; full also checks A/V offset at every join and writes before/after PNGs.

tools.description: Tool paths. Empty: ROSTRUM_FFMPEG / ROSTRUM_FFPROBE, then PATH.

init.description: How `rostrum init <folder>` turns files into talks.

partPattern.description: On the file stem: files whose stems match are parts of one talk, in the order of capture group 1 (the part number, required); the rest of the stem names the talk. Every other file is a talk of its own.

mediaExtensions.description: Files with these extensions are picked up from a folder. A source needs both video and audio.
